# GLP-1 Receptor Agonists — Cardiovascular Outcomes Review

## Background
GLP-1 receptor agonists, originally developed for type 2 diabetes, demonstrate
profound cardiovascular benefits in trials including LEADER, SUSTAIN-6, and SELECT.

## Mechanism of Action
Activation of GLP-1 receptors on pancreatic beta cells enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion
and suppresses glucagon. Cardiovascular benefit appears partly weight-loss-mediated and partly
direct via vascular GLP-1 receptors and reduced inflammation.

## Trials
SELECT trial in non-diabetic obese adults showed 20% MACE reduction with semaglutide 2.4mg.
SURMOUNT-1 demonstrated 22.5% weight loss with tirzepatide.

## Safety Signals
GI side effects (nausea 44%, vomiting 24%) drive discontinuation. Pancreatitis signal
remains under surveillance but unconfirmed in meta-analyses. Thyroid C-cell tumors only seen in rodents.

## Conclusions
GLP-1 agonists are now first-line for obese type 2 diabetics with cardiovascular risk,
and increasingly used off-label in obesity without diabetes.
